Given a question and an answer, analyze the complexity of each sentence in the answer. Break down each sentence into one or more fully understandable statements. Ensure that no pronouns are used in any statement. Format the outputs in JSON.
Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}
Output: {
    "statements": [
        "Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.",
        "Albert Einstein is recognized as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.",
        "Albert Einstein was best known for developing the theory of relativity.",
        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
    ]
}
-----------------------------

Now perform the same with the following input
input: {
    "question": "user: What options are available for a home loan with poor credit but a good rental history?\nassistant: Sorry, but I do not know. \nuser: Are there any options available that require no down payment?\nassistant: Yes. If you're in the US, several options allow you to buy a home with little to no down payment. However, you will still need some funds for closing costs, which can often be negotiated with the seller. \nOne option is an FHA loan, which requires a down payment of only 3.5%. The US government effectively subsidizes the remainder of your down payment. Other options include 80/20 loans, which provide 100% coverage, and HUD assistance programs, which can help you secure a 100% loan through FHA.\nuser: Can I get an FHA loan if I have a low credit score?\nassistant: Yes, you can qualify for their loan programs with a credit score as low as 580.\nuser: Do I need to pay for PMI with an FHA loan?\nassistant: Private mortgage insurance (PMI) is required for FHA loans with less than 20% equity. PMI must accompany FHA-insured loans because the FHA element serves as the insurance. The FHA does not provide the loan; instead, it insures the loan on behalf of a lender. This arrangement comes at a cost to the borrower. Still, it allows individuals who may struggle to afford a traditional mortgage to qualify, thanks to lower payment requirements and a reduced PMI.\nuser: What is MMI or Mutual Mortgage Insurance?\nassistant: MI stands for Mortgage Insurance, which is a generic term. FHA refers to MMI, or Mutual Mortgage Insurance. \nuser: Is there a maximum income limit to qualify?\nassistant: I do not know if there is a maximum income limit for qualifying for an FHA loan.\nuser: What about the rent-to-buy option?",
    "answer": "Rent-to-buy typically involves paying an upfront deposit or premium—separate from a security deposit—to purchase the right to buy the home later at a specified price. You will often also pay rent above the market rate. That extra rent may be contractually credited toward the purchase price; the document notes that many people recommend having it applied specifically toward the down payment. [S3]\n\nSo, it is not necessarily a no-upfront-payment option. The document does not establish whether poor credit affects eligibility, whether your rental history helps, or whether the arrangement guarantees you can obtain financing when it is time to buy. [S3]"
}
